copy.blurb:
This is a Pick. Mexico v Korea Republic in FIFA World Cup 2026 on Friday, and the model and the market disagree on the Korea Republic side by +10.5pp. That's the gap the verdict rests on.

On Elo, Mexico comes in 60 points ahead — Mexico at 1830, Korea Republic at 1770. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. The adjustment layer is quiet on this fixture — no host bonus, no home-ground correction, no altitude folding in. The Elo numbers above are what the model uses.

Three-way split from the model: Mexico to win at 43%, the draw at 26%, and Korea Republic to win at 31%. Each number is a probability over the full range of plausible in-form, no-injury, ninety-minute scenarios — not a prediction of a scoreline.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Mexico to win at 53%, the draw at 27%, and Korea Republic to win at 20%. The Korea Republic side trades at 20% on Polymarket, which prices out at American odds of +400. That's where the engine differs: our number reads 31%, +10.5pp wider.

Pick gate is a lower-bound check, not the point estimate. A 100-sample bootstrap perturbs the Elo prior (±20), the host bonus (±15), and the altitude bonus (±10), then reads the 5th-percentile probability back out. On the Korea Republic side that lower bound is 25% — +5.4pp clear of the market's 20%, comfortably past our +3pp threshold. The engine isn't arguing reputation, recency, or narrative. It's reading the underlying numbers and finding Korea Republic priced shorter on the market than the prior supports — that's the disagreement.

What would close this gap: confirmed team news that pulls the prior down on the side we like, a venue or weather change, or a tournament suspension landing before kickoff. With kickoff 27 days out, refresh is weekly; daily cadence picks up inside the final five days. A Pick this wide doesn't collapse on small news; a narrow one can flip to Pass on a single refresh. Either way, the engine republishes and the page reflects the latest read.
drivers: The +10.5pp gap clears the Desk's 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
This is a selection call on the Korea Republic side, not a blanket read on the market.
Confirmed XI, fitness news, and weather re-enter the prior closer to kickoff.
Bootstrap lower-bound on the Korea Republic side still clears the Pick threshold.
copy.summary: The model thinks Korea Republic are mispriced. Our number reads 31% on the away side; the market reads 20%. The +10.5pp gap is the Pick.
copy.title: Mexico v Korea Republic · the model leans Korea Republic
